_comment: All the settings you can change without touching the code. Edit the numbers here, save, restart the app.
_source_help: Path to your demo video. Use the number 0 instead (no quotes) to use your webcam.
_loop_video_help: When the video ends, start it again. Handy during a live demo.
_device_help: Use 'cpu' unless you have an NVIDIA GPU set up, then use 0.
_confidence_help: How sure YOLO must be before it calls something a person. Lower = more detections but more false positives.
_process_width_help: Frames are shrunk to this width before detection. This mainly sets the size of the picture shown in the dashboard - it is NOT the speed knob, because YOLO resizes to 'imgsz' internally anyway. Lower it to cut bandwidth, not to gain frame rate.
_frame_skip_help: Skip this many frames between detections. Raise to 1 or 2 if your laptop is slow.
_dwell_alert_help: Alert when one person stays in a zone longer than this.
_alert_cooldown_help: After an alert fires, wait this long before firing the same one again (stops alert spam).

heatmap._decay_help: How fast old footsteps fade. 0.99 = long trails, 0.90 = only recent movement.
heatmap._intensity_help: How strongly the heatmap colours are blended over the video.

_zones_help: Draw these on the dashboard with 'Edit zones'. A normal zone alerts when it goes over capacity (Track A). A restricted zone alerts when ANYONE is inside it (Track B intrusion). Every shape is stored the same way: an ordered list of [x, y] points in the frame's own pixel coordinates.
_flow_help: Movement arrows. columns/rows set the grid; decay is how fast old motion fades; min_speed ignores people standing still.
_app_name_help: Shown on the boot screen and in the header.
_units_help: Response units for Track B dispatch. Positions are pixels in the processed frame, the same coordinate space as zone points. You do not need to edit these by hand: press EDIT UNITS on the site map, drag the markers, and press SAVE UNITS.
_imgsz_help: THE setting that controls speed. YOLO resizes frames to this before running the network. Measured on the demo clip: 640 -> 15 fps, 512 -> 27 fps (same accuracy), 416 -> 35 fps, 320 -> 53 fps but starts missing people. Lower it if you need speed; re-measure, because the right value depends on how small people are in your frame.
_zones_frame_width_help: The frame width the zone points were drawn at. If you change process_width, run.py rescales the zones automatically so they still cover the same part of the scene.
_auto_zone_on_start_help: Off by default. When true, a video that loads with no zones is analysed and a zone is proposed over the busy area. The AUTO button in the zone editor does the same thing on demand, which is usually what you want: you decide what is worth monitoring.
